# VaccineInjuries.org

> VaccineInjuries.org is an independent educational and connection website. It explains, in plain English, the two U.S. federal programs that compensate people for serious vaccine injuries — the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) and the Countermeasures Injury Compensation Program (CICP) — and, on request, connects people who believe they had a serious vaccine reaction with independent attorneys so they can discuss their options. It is not a law firm and not a government agency, and nothing on the site is legal or medical advice.

Key facts the site explains (always confirm against the official sources below):

- Serious vaccine injuries are uncommon. Filing a claim is how the federal no-fault system is designed to work; the site is not anti-vaccine.
- The VICP covers vaccines the CDC recommends for routine use in children or pregnant women that are subject to a federal excise tax (for example seasonal flu, Tdap/DTaP, MMR, HPV, hepatitis A and B, pneumococcal conjugate, varicella). Petitions are decided by special masters of the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.
- VICP filing deadlines: generally within 3 years of the first symptom of the injury; for a death, within 2 years of the death and 4 years of the first symptom of the injury that led to it.
- VICP severity requirement: effects lasting more than 6 months, or inpatient hospitalization with surgery, or death.
- The Vaccine Injury Table (42 CFR 100.3) lists injuries (such as anaphylaxis, SIRVA, vasovagal syncope, brachial neuritis, and Guillain-Barré syndrome after seasonal flu vaccine) with onset windows; meeting the Table creates a presumption of causation. Off-Table injuries require proof of causation.
- COVID-19 vaccine injury claims go to the CICP, which generally has a 1-year filing deadline from the date of vaccination, does not pay attorney fees, and does not pay pain and suffering.
- Reporting to VAERS is a safety report, not a compensation claim, and does not stop any filing deadline.

## Injury guides

Each guide covers symptoms and onset, whether and how the injury appears on the Vaccine Injury Table (quoting 42 CFR 100.3), filing deadlines, and helpful records.

- [All injury guides](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries)
- [SIRVA (shoulder injury related to vaccine administration)](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/sirva): on the Table for most injected vaccines, pain within 48 hours
- [Guillain-Barré syndrome](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/guillain-barre-syndrome): on the Table for seasonal flu vaccines, 3-42 days
- [Transverse myelitis](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/transverse-myelitis): not on the Table (off-Table claim)
- [CIDP](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/cidp): not on the Table; excluded from Table GBS
- [Brachial neuritis](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/brachial-neuritis): on the Table for tetanus toxoid-containing vaccines, 2-28 days
- [Anaphylaxis](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/anaphylaxis): on the Table for many covered vaccines, within 4 hours
- [ITP / thrombocytopenic purpura](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/itp-thrombocytopenic-purpura): on the Table for measles-containing vaccines, 7-30 days
- [Fainting (vasovagal syncope) injuries](https://www.vaccineinjuries.org/injuries/syncope-fainting): on the Table for injected vaccines, within 1 hour
